rule_or_pattern: on this dev book drop the roll-call vote-table lines: labels containing a dot-leader run (regex `(\.{2,}|[·•]\s?[·•])`) or ending in a standalone vote mark (regex `\s[ONΟΝ0]$`), plus any line flagged C:cpp_vs_book_out or C:repeated_word; keep the prose lines
notes: The prose pages (1-9, 15) are clean polytonic and correct. About half the book is roll-call vote tables (page.jpg p000016: two name columns with dot leaders and Ν/Ο vote marks). Names are mostly read right, but the leaders are transcribed with arbitrary dot counts and mixed '.'/'·'/'•' (10, 16, 24, 26, 34, 40). The vote letters come out as Latin 'N'/'O' or digit '0' (17, 27, 28; 'Ο' vs '0' on page.jpg), and two lines are junk: 21 doubles 'Καζαμπάκας', and 22 reads 'г. Γ. Мо Μαυρομιχάλης' with Cyrillic г/М. As dev/eval data these table rows add CER noise from leaders and homoglyphs rather than reading skill. If the table rows are wanted for training, the minimum fix is to drop 21-22 and relabel standalone Latin N/O to Greek Ν/Ο.
